common_mistakes: Pouring footings before the footing inspection — Pittsburgh inspectors will want to see open holes before concrete goes in
Submitting a deck plan without ledger flashing and attachment details — this is one of the most common review delays
Using undersized or non-approved connectors/fasteners instead of corrosion-resistant hardware approved for exterior deck framing
Assuming the $14,000 job value means the permit fee will be $84 — Pittsburgh's $130 minimum applies, so the minimum fee still controls
Skipping Pennsylvania HIC registration verification for a contractor on a job over $5,000

pro_tips: Open the footing holes and call for inspection before any concrete is poured — this saves the most time and avoids the most common failed inspection.
Submit a complete deck framing package up front: ledger, flashing, footing depth, beam/post sizes, and guard details. Missing ledger details are the #1 reason deck permits stall.
Because the job value is over $5,000, verify the contractor's Pennsylvania HIC registration before you submit anything — it is a common rejection point for residential work.
If the deck will ever support a roof, pergola, hot tub, or heavy planters, include that load in the design now; retrofitting later usually means a new permit revision.
